paragraphs: The administrative law judges on this page correspond to the combined occupation under United States O*NET 23-1021.00, comprising Administrative Law Judges, Adjudicators and Hearing Officers. The work converts the case file, the law, the evidence and the hearing record into a procedural decision or written reasons; the real thresholds are neutrality, lawful authority, completeness of the record and reviewability, and it cannot be mapped directly onto a single Chinese occupation. Mainland China also has no comparable sub-occupational national wage distribution.

Suits people who can stay self-controlled when the parties make opposing statements, read case files for long periods, separate facts from assertions, allow the other side to respond, and write conclusions whose reasons a higher authority or a court can review. If you would rather fight for one side's outcome, dislike procedural constraints, or find delay and emotional conflict hard to handle, try a simulated hearing first; record how you handle being interrupted, insufficient evidence and an unfavourable conclusion.

Use a fictional welfare-eligibility case as a 60-minute sample: first check recusal, list the issues and the burden of proof, preside over both parties' statements, rule on two evidentiary objections, then write a one-page decision containing the facts, the rules, the reasoning and the notice of review. Afterwards, have a peer check it item by item for notification, opportunity to respond, evidentiary basis and traceability of reasons; also write down one moment when you wanted to strengthen an argument for one side but should have stayed neutral, and explain how you would turn that impulse into a question pending verification.

United States ALJs, agency hearing officers and related Chinese job titles are similar in name, so the jurisdiction, the appointment, the legal qualification and the final decision authority must still be verified.

The work of administrative law judges can be divided into three categories: presiding over proceedings, examining the case file and the evidence, and producing a reviewable decision; the specific final signing authority is determined by the agency's authorization.

Conduct case triage and conflict-of-interest checks, identify the issues, the law and the burden of proof, arrange hearings and notices, preside over statements, witness examination and evidentiary objections, maintain a complete record and state the review or appeal route.

entries: Materials｜Pre-hearing case file preparation｜Verify the application, the agency decision, witness statements, medical or employment records, expert opinions, statutes and precedents, and organize locatable issues and evidence.

Hearing｜Hearings and procedural management｜Arrange notices and scheduling, preside over statements, witness examination and evidentiary objections; handle interpretation, technical failures and the parties' opportunity to respond at the same time.

Neutrality｜Neutral adjudicative role｜Not a lawyer representing either party, nor a mediator who merely facilitates settlement; manage the record under the authorized procedure and make or recommend a judgment whose reasons can be stated.

Context｜Case scope and tempo｜May hear social programme eligibility, occupational licensing, environmental or health and safety matters; caseload and time limits are affected by the procedure, the parties and the agency's resources.

Quality｜Procedural quality and review｜Quality includes recusal and notification, the opportunity for both parties to be heard, completeness of the record, correspondence between facts and law, clarity of reasons, and the time limits and review outcome.

Process｜The administrative adjudication work cycle｜Triage and recusal checks, identifying the issues and the burden of proof, notifying and holding hearings, reviewing the evidence, maintaining the record, forming reasons and stating the review route.

Adjacent occupations may share legal research, procedural management, case-file organization and communication abilities, but the representation relationship, adjudicative authority, appointment qualification, confidentiality duties and review route are not the same. When choosing a direction, verify the actual authorization of the target role rather than judging only by the job title or legal training.

A job title alone cannot demonstrate authority. Before comparing, verify who is responsible for presiding over hearings, who may sign the final decision, whether one may only make recommendations, which recusal and confidentiality rules apply, and whether the decision will be reviewed internally by the agency, by an administrative review body or by a court. entries.answer: This combined occupation revolves around researching the case file, the applicable law and the procedural rules in an administrative dispute; the work may include arranging or supporting hearings, handling objections, verifying evidence and notification, forming a traceable record, and drafting decisions, recommendations or draft reasons. Around the hearing, work is also arranged around deadlines, service, recusal, the parties' opportunity to respond and completeness of the record; when new material, interpretation or a technical problem arises, the handling must follow the specific agency's procedure. Whether one may preside over hearings, find facts or sign depends on the agency, the jurisdiction, the appointment document and the scope of authorization; the work of a support role must not be mistaken for independent adjudicative authority.

entries.answer: The appointment source, jurisdiction, presiding scope and final signing authority of a court judge, a federal ALJ, an agency adjudicator and a hearing officer are not the same; a mediator usually facilitates negotiation and a lawyer usually represents one party, neither of which equals a neutral adjudicator. Legal research, case management or enforcement experience builds procedural ability but does not automatically produce authority to preside over hearings, find facts or issue decisions. Before applying for any position, the target agency's announcement and the statutory authorization must govern.

entries.answer: Within the approved material scope, AI can assist with retrieving public rules, organizing a timeline, comparing versions or structuring a draft, but the output may omit facts, mis-cite rules or amplify bias in the input, and therefore cannot be equated with adjudicative authorization or a legal conclusion. It also cannot replace the real-time management of both parties' statements in a hearing, or the responsibility to write the applicable rules and evidence locations into reviewable reasons. Recusal judgment, evidence handling, fact-finding, procedural fairness and the reasons for the decision must be reviewed by personnel with authority in that jurisdiction, and the basis must be retained. Before use, also confirm whether the material may be input, whether the supplier and tool are approved, how versions are preserved and who is responsible for the final output; without explicit authorization, the scope of use should not be expanded on the grounds of “improving efficiency”.
